record.context_brief: closure operator on irreducible subset systems
record.original_question: Let H be the partially ordered collection of irreducible subset systems on Top0, let HR be the induced irreducible subset system of H-Rudin sets, and define R : H -> H by R(H) = HR. If H has property M, must R be a closure operator, that is, monotone, expansive, and idempotent?

evidence.quote: Question 1.9. Let H : Top0 -> Set be an R-subset system having property M. Is R : H -> H, H 7-> HR a closure operator?
A map c : P -> P is called a closure operator (on P) if, for all x, y in P, (1) x <= y implies c(x) <= c(y), (2) x <= c(x), (3) c(c(x)) = c(x).
Let HR(X) = {A subset X | A has H-Rudin property}. The sets in HR(X) will also be called H-Rudin sets.
Theorem 4.15. Let H : Top0 -> Set be an R-subset system. Then R : H -> H, defined by H 7-> HR is a closure operator.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

Let $\mathbf{Top}_0$ denote the category of $T_0$ topological spaces and continuous maps, and let $\mathbf{Set}$ denote the category of sets. For a $T_0$ space $X$, write $\mathcal{P}(X)$ for the power set of $X$ and let $\mathrm{Irr}(X) \subseteq \mathcal{P}(X)$ denote the family of nonempty irreducible closed subsets of $X$ (a closed set $C$ is irreducible if it is nonempty and cannot be written as a union of two proper closed subsets).

A subset system on $\mathbf{Top}_0$ is a functor $H : \mathbf{Top}_0 \to \mathbf{Set}$ such that for every $X \in \mathbf{Top}_0$, $H(X) \subseteq \mathcal{P}(X)$, and for every continuous map $f : X \to Y$, $H(f)(A) = f(A)$ for all $A \in H(X)$. An irreducible subset system is a subset system $H$ such that for every $X$, every member of $H(X)$ is an irreducible subset of $X$ (i.e., its closure is irreducible). Let $\mathbb{H}$ denote the partially ordered collection of all irreducible subset systems on $\mathbf{Top}_0$, ordered by pointwise inclusion: $H \le H'$ iff $H(X) \subseteq H'(X)$ for every $X$.

For an irreducible subset system $H$ and $X \in \mathbf{Top}_0$, a subset $A \subseteq X$ is said to have the $H$-Rudin property if for every closed set $C \subseteq X$ with $A \subseteq C$, there exists $B \in H(X)$ with $B \subseteq A$ and $\overline{B} \subseteq C$ (equivalently, $\overline{A}$ is a minimal closed set among those containing some member of $H(X)$ in a suitable sense). Define
$$H_R(X) = \{ A \subseteq X : A \text{ has the } H\text{-Rudin property} \}.$$
The assignment $X \mapsto H_R(X)$ defines a new irreducible subset system $H_R$, called the induced subset system of $H$-Rudin sets.

Define a map $R : \mathbb{H} \to \mathbb{H}$ by $R(H) = H_R$.

A map $c : P \to P$ on a poset $P$ is a closure operator if for all $x,y \in P$: (1) $x \le y \Rightarrow c(x) \le c(y)$ (monotone), (2) $x \le c(x)$ (expansive), (3) $c(c(x)) = c(x)$ (idempotent).

Property M. An irreducible subset system $H$ is said to have property $M$ if for every $T_0$ space $X$ and every $A \in H(X)$, the closure $\overline{A}$ contains a smallest member of $H(X)$ in $A$ in the sense required for the Rudin construction to behave naturally (more precisely: for every continuous map $f$ and every $A$ in $H$, the image-related compatibility needed for $H_R$ to inherit functoriality holds).

Question. Suppose $H$ is an irreducible subset system on $\mathbf{Top}_0$ with property $M$. Is the map $R : \mathbb{H} \to \mathbb{H}$, $H \mapsto H_R$, necessarily a closure operator on $\mathbb{H}$?

artifact.status_search_result: The question receives a positive answer in the same work where it is posed: a theorem establishes that for every R-subset system H on Top_0, the map H ↦ H_R is a closure operator (monotone, expansive, idempotent), affirmatively answering the question.

status_evidence.snippet: Theorem 4.15. Let H : Top0 -> Set be an R-subset system. Then R : H -> H, defined by H ↦ H_R is a closure operator.
status_evidence.claim: The question of whether R is a closure operator is answered affirmatively in the paper.
